title: Austin City Hall Construction & Street Improvements 1906
summary:
• **New City Hall Project Moving Forward** – Council approved a $2,875 excavation contract with James Bergen and authorized $362.25 for architectural plans and specifications for the new city hall building.

• **Street and Infrastructure Upgrades** – Funded $100 for cemetery improvements and authorized a work crew (1 team and 2 men) to clean gutters and spread dirt throughout the city.

• **Failed Skating Ban** – A proposed ordinance prohibiting skateboarding on sidewalks was defeated, with 7 aldermen voting against the restriction.

• **Multiple Budget Approvals** – Council approved approximately $2,057 in various expenditures, including $518.23 and $1,177.21 for approved street department accounts and $40 to compensate a prisoner guard.

• **Business Permits Mixed Results** – Council denied one platform construction request (W.S. Walkers & Sons on West 3rd Street) but approved another for W.B. Wackert & Sons at their main business location under street committee supervision.

Austin Texas Sept 17th 1906
Hon W O Shelley Mayor presiding
Roll Called

Reports of City Officers
The Mayor laid before the Council the report of the City Attorney, which was on motion
referred to the Finance Committee without reading.
Reports of Standing Committees
Alderman Petri for the claims & accounts Committee to whom was referred the petition of
J.E. Maddax in regard to fees presented a report recommending that the petition be
granted. On motion the report was adopted.
Alderman Wilhelm for the Cemetery Committee to whom was referred the report of the Sexton
for the month of Aug 1906, presented a report stating that same had been examined and
found correct
On motion the report was adopted.
Reports of Special Committees
Alderman Moore for the Special City Hall Committee made a verbal report stating that under
instructions from the Council they had advertised for and received bids for the excavation
at the New City Hall, and recommended the acceptance of the bid of Jas Bergen for the sum
of $2875.00 also that they had arranged with two G.R. Fannell for rent of stalls for City
Mules. at a rental of $10.00 per mule, also that they had arranged for quarters for the
Mayor. On motion the recommendations of the Committee were adopted and ratified.
